narration_timeline.text: Look at this mantis lifting one front leg as it moves in front of the camera.
narration_timeline.scene: A live mantis nymph visibly waving a foreleg

narration_timeline.text: Those folded forelegs carry tiny spines that help hold objects close to its body.
Other recordings show a mantis gripping insect prey with those very same front legs.
narration_timeline.scene: Mantis holding real captured insect prey

narration_timeline.text: On a quiet leaf, a mantis can pause and carefully reposition its forelegs.
In another outdoor scene, a mantis reacts by raising its arms in a wider posture.
narration_timeline.scene: Mantis response in separate outdoor footage

narration_timeline.text: From a small wave to gripping prey, these forelegs do much more than walking.
narration_timeline.scene: Raised mantis forelegs plus another close study
